routes.label: Count by the two free digits

question: A palindrome between \(1000\) and \(10{,}000\) is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by \(7?\)
solution:
Every palindrome in the given interval has digits \(abba\), where \(a\) is one of \(1,2,\ldots,9\) and \(b\) is one of \(0,1,\ldots,9\). Each pair \((a,b)\) gives exactly one palindrome, and every eligible palindrome gives exactly one such pair. There are therefore \(9\cdot10=90\) possibilities.

The value of this palindrome is
\[
P=1001a+110b.
\]
To test divisibility by \(7\), use \(1001=7\cdot143\) and \(110=7\cdot16-2\). Then
\[
P=7(143a+16b)-2b.
\]
The first term is a multiple of \(7\), so \(P\) is divisible by \(7\) exactly when \(2b\) is divisible by \(7\). Because \(b\) is a digit, \(2b\) is even and lies between \(0\) and \(18\). The multiples of \(7\) in this interval are \(0,7,14\); only \(0\) and \(14\) are even. Thus \(b=0\) or \(b=7\).

Either choice of \(b\) works with all \(9\) choices of \(a\), giving \(18\) distinct favorable palindromes. Since the \(90\) palindromes are equally likely, the probability is
\[
\frac{18}{90}=\frac15,
\]
choice E.
